title: DFTracer: An Analysis-Friendly Data Flow Tracer for AI-Driven Workflows
problem: Modern HPC workflows integrating simulation, data analytics, and AI applications require performance analysis tools that trace multiple software stack layers, but current tools (Score-P, Recorder, Darshan) cannot handle AI-based I/O stacks and fail to capture I/O from dynamically spawned processes.
motivation: Comprehensive understanding of data exchange patterns in AI-driven HPC workflows is essential to improve time to scientific insight.
method: DFTracer uses three mechanisms: (1) a unified interface that intercepts data-centric events at multiple software stack layers, (2) an optimized trace format enabling efficient loading of multi-million events in seconds, and (3) an event tagging system associating low-level I/O operations with high-level workflow context for domain-centric analysis.
key_novelty: Unified multi-layer tracing interface with workflow-specific context tagging for comprehensive performance analysis of AI-driven HPC workflows.
contributions: Unified interface capturing trace data from multiple software stack layers simultaneously
Analysis-friendly trace format optimized for efficient loading of multi-million events
Workflow context tagging enabling domain-centric data flow analysis
1.44x smaller runtime overhead and 1.3-7.1x smaller trace size than existing tools

metrics.speedup: 3 orders of magnitude faster loading for 100M events

primary_theme: Performance tracing for AI-driven HPC workflows
